newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan phosphates firm in $220 mln Pakistani deal.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan phosphates firm in $220 mln Pakistani deal.

text.p: Morocco's Office Cherifien des Phosphates (OCP), the world's main exporter of phosphates and by-products, has signed a $220 million deal with Pakistan to set up a fertiliser plant in Karachi.
An OCP statement, carried by the official news agency MAP, said the joint venture agreement was signed earlier this week with Al Noor Fertilizer Industries Ltd.
The deal was part of OCP's new policy of forging international partnerships, it said.
OCP will keep 10 percent of the capital and meet all the plant's demands for phosphoric acid from Morocco which at present prices represented turnover of some $80 million.
The $220 million plant, due to come on stream in 1998, will have a daily production capacity of 1,300 tonnes of fertiliser, 1,200 tonnes of urea and 955 tonnes of ammoniac.
OCP will provide technical and marketing advice and the Manila-based Asian Development Bank, and Britain's Export Credit Guarantee Department will take part in financing the deal, the statement said.
The Moroccan company's shipments of phosphates and by-products in 1995 totalled 10 billion dirhams ($1.15 billion).
